Welcome to our Pre-Prep and Nursery for children aged 2 to 7
Hazlegrove Pre-Prep provides children with a wonderful start to school life.
Our Pre-Prep is run by caring, creative and experienced staff who know exactly how to bring out the best in each pupil, and, most importantly, make learning fun! As part of the Hazlegrove school our Pre-Prep children have access to an amazing array of resources including our 25m indoor swimming pool, theatre, dance studio and sports pitches.
We have excellent resources and the flexibility to deliver the curriculum in a way that helps our children learn and consolidate that knowledge with practical experiments and activities. Our days are balanced with academic learning of key maths and literacy taking place in the morning, whilst afternoons are filled with creative and practical work including Science, Art, PE, Dance, Drama, Music, French and our popular Forest School sessions.
The chance to take part in such a wide variety of activities from a young age helps children discover the talents and passions that define them, feel proud of their achievements and develop confidence in their abilities. We aim to give the children in our Nursery and Pre-Prep the very best start to their school lives.
The support our youngest child has received since starting the school this September has been exceptional

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to our Prep | Hazlegrove School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to our Prep
Hazlegrove is an exceptional coeducational full boarding and day school where we enable children to be children and are committed to celebrating childhood.
We are largely an ‘unplugged’ school, you won't see our children (or staff!) walking around with mobile phones because we believe that education is about learning all of the essential skills needed to communicate successfully with those alongside us and build a strong sense of self-belief. Computers and ICT are seen as a vital component of Hazlegrove education but never as an end in themselves.
Nurturing the Whole Child
The Prep School, for Years 3 to 8, offers an enriching, all-round education where the rigours of the curriculum sit alongside the values and ethos that underpin life at Hazlegrove. We want our pupils to embrace the school values of kindness, respect, integrity, grace, generosity and courage.
A vibrant and creative curriculum, exceptional pastoral care and stunning rural Somerset location combine to make children feel nurtured, motivated, inspired and encouraged to love learning for life.
It's all about the ‘Three Cs’ at Hazlegrove! Hazlegrovians are curious, creative and confident when they leave us at the end of Year 8, keen to make the most of all of the opportunities on offer to them.
The Prep Curriculum
The curriculum has a real, hands-on sense to it, where children participate fully and are not just spectators. We are passionate about developing in the children, genuine awe, wonder and curiosity at the complexities of life and the world about us - past, present and future.
The breadth and balance in the curriculum give pupils an opportunity to get excited about the lessons they have each day. Activity and investigation enable pupils to learn to think for themselves and to solve problems. We hope that they can begin to see that failure and getting it wrong are just as important as getting it right.
Preparing for the Next Phase
The heart of prep school education is expressed in one word, preparatory. The curriculum at Hazlegrove prepares children for the next phases of their lives, for the demands of a more specialised senior education and, in the longer term, to be able to meet the challenges of the workplace and to thrive in their personal and professional lives, understanding their responsibilities in making the world a better place. In Year 4, pupils join the rest of the Prep School in attending school on Saturday mornings from which the children benefit in a myriad of ways; whether it be the space this creates over the course of a week to explore topics and interests to the pressure that this removes from having to fit everything in from Monday to Friday.

Extra-Curricular Activities
The traditional academic disciplines, including Latin, are complimented by Music and Drama, Art and Design and Outdoor Education, as well as a varied Sports programme. Computers and ICT are seen as a vital component of Hazlegrove education but never as an end in themselves.
Humanities take place in the Fitzjames building, a fantastic, flexible and innovative addition to the teaching space whose light, bright classrooms open on to first floor gallery and full height atrium where a huge globe hangs from the ceiling; broad steps double as informal seating.
Progress and Assessment
Pupils' progress is monitored from an early age to ensure that potential is fulfilled and any difficulties are identified as early as possible. This progress is regularly assessed, both formally and informally, and parents are kept up-to-date about levels of effort and attainment through the reporting system and pattern of regular parent-teacher meetings. Parents are encouraged to discuss their children's progress with staff at any time.
Pupils are prepared for entry to a wide range of senior schools and considerable success is achieved on the scholarship front. They gain entry either through the Common Entrance or Scholarship examinations and awards gained may be Academic, Sport, Music, Art, DT, Drama or All Round.
Prep School Structure
Find out more about the structure of the prep school
The tutor is the first point of contact for pupils and parents if there are academic or other concerns. Additionally, the Head of Section (Lower School, Middle School or Upper School) will always be happy to discuss any concerns parents may have.
In Years 3 and 4, the class teacher is the tutor.
In Years 5 and 6 the children are taught by specialist teachers for the majority of subject but still have a "class teacher" for English and humanities. All children in a Year 5 class have the same tutor who they meet in the mornings and at the end of lunchtimes for registration and for longer tutor periods.
In Years 7 and 8 the tutor groups become "House" based rather than class based and all subjects are taught by specialist teachers.
Children are taught throughout the school in mixed ability, parallel classes, with some setting in French and Maths. In Years 7 and 8, pupils are either prepared for Common Entrance or in a higher tier stream where pupils are prepared for academic scholarship.
Prep is set for pupils in Years 5 to 8 on four nights of the week (Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday), younger pupils will be expected to read, learn spellings and practise times tables.
Years 3 - 6
In Years 3 - 6, the academic reward is the Plus Point. A member of staff might give up to three Plus Points to a child for a particular deed. The total of Plus Points a child gets in a week is calculated by the house staff and goes towards an overall house total, which in turn forms part of the overall annual House Competition.
For academic work, the major reward is the Merit. A Merit wins three extra plus points for the House. These are awarded by staff for exceptional work by the individual child. The child’s tutor keeps a record of the Merits for the term.
Years 7 and 8
In Years 7 and 8 pupils move to a system of Commendations. A Commendation is awarded for work that is exceptional for the individual child in terms of effort or attainment. At the end of each term the highest scoring pupils are awarded a book token in final assembly. Tutors can also award a ‘wild card’ to pupils who have made exceptional progress.
ShowHM
All children are encouraged to earn a ShowHM! These are pieces of work that the teacher thinks the pupil should show to the Headmaster, this is then mentioned in our weekly Celebration Assembly and the children achieve the coveted 'ShowHM stamp.
There are four "Houses" in the Prep School at Hazlegrove which are Dover (red), Lyon (blue), Norton (yellow) and Tremlett (green). Houses are allocated on joining the Prep School and children in the same immediate family will belong to the same House. The children wear House ties during the winter terms.
Inter-house competitions run throughout the year in sport and other areas of school life.
We are so happy with Hazlegrove and feel very blessed that our children have the opportunity to learn in such a wonderfully inspiring setting

Headmaster's Welcome to Hazlegrove
Great Stories Begin at Hazlegrove Prep School.
It is my great privilege and honour to be the Headmaster of Hazlegrove, and a pleasure to welcome you to this wonderful school. The values and charms of a country boarding prep school are as prevalent today as they have ever been, and Hazlegrove is at the forefront of this. We provide an environment where children can be children, enjoy the great outdoors, and develop a profound sense of curiosity, creativity and confidence.
Amidst our glorious 200 acres of grounds, we are blessed with many wonderful facilities such as our state-of the art Teaching and Learning centre, sports hall, indoor swimming pool, art and DT facilities, and theatre. These undoubtedly help put Hazlegrove into the leading category of schools in the UK. We are a day and boarding school in which a family ethos is at its very core. As a parent of boarding children, I am more than aware of the faith you invest in entrusting us to look after your children. We pride ourselves in our outstanding pastoral care, applying a proactive rather than reactive approach, in which every member of staff, whatever their role, is involved.
We also pride ourselves in our all-round excellence, and our pupils achieve awards in a variety of different disciplines to a range of the top senior schools in the country. However, learning goes well beyond the classroom. Our greatest desire is to provide as many opportunities and experiences for each child, so that they can discover their own unique skills and talents and develop into curious and passionate learners.
...we want our children to become kind, confident and self-assured young people...
We believe that every child is a human being with immeasurable potential and it is our goal at Hazlegrove to find and nurture that potential. Integral to our nurturing environment is our “no-phone” policy, which has always been adhered to at Hazlegrove, both by our pupils and as importantly by our staff. We do, of course, promote and educate the use of technology through our curriculum, but we also recognise that separation from a personal phone use plays a key part in protecting our children from the pitfalls of social media and addictive behaviour patterns.
We want to ensure that they have the social, emotional and academic foundations to go on to thrive at senior school and beyond, equipped with a strong sense of the '3Cs': Curiosity, Creativity and Confidence. Ultimately, we want our children to become kind, confident and self-assured young people, in the backdrop of this unique, nurturing and inspirational school.
My wife Amanda and I look forward to welcoming you to Hazlegrove soon in order to show you this exciting school and share with you our vision and aims.
Ed Benbow Headmaster
More about Ed and Amanda
Ed and Amanda live on-site at Hazlegrove with their children, Eli and Freddie, and two lively cocker spaniels, Pickle and Muffin. Both Ed and Amanda are passionate about the family boarding ethos that is central to Hazlegrove’s philosophy having both attended full boarding schools. They play an active part in the boarding community, working alongside the gaps and boarding staff to ensure children thrive and that parents feel a valued part of our school community. They fully immerse themselves in as many areas of the School as possible and are actively involved with all children from Nursery to Year 8, sharing a common desire to ignite the fire in every child.
It’s a place where children work and play hard, but where they also as importantly have bucketloads of fun and stay children until they leave at 13.

Prep school boarding at its best
Great Stories Begin With A Village...
The Heart of our Community
At Hazlegrove our boarders are the heartbeat of the school and with our thriving community of both full boarders as well as flexi boarders, at least one third of the Prep School are boarding at any one time. Many of our boarding families choose Hazlegrove on the strength of personal recommendations from past and current pupils.
We offer an exciting full weekend programme of activities that take place both on and off site including trips to water parks, the beach, fishing trips, exhibitions and museums, zorb balls, disco domes, tree climbing not to mention our very own Go-Kart track and outdoor pizza oven!
Boarding at Hazlegrove provides a home-from-home for the children within a family focussed, supportive and inclusive community. It’s of paramount importance to us that your children feel safe and happy staying here. You can be confident that our experienced houseparents and boarding staff will take care of your child’s physical and emotional wellbeing, ensuring they have a relaxed and fun time at our school
It’s a wonderful opportunity for your child to reach their potential, grow in confidence and make friends and memories that will last a lifetime.
Pastoral care is key to the strength and overall success of the boarding at Hazlegrove; it is at the heart of everything that we do.
Our boarding staff meet every week to discuss the welfare of our boarders supported by continual communication with tutors and staff.
Pastoral care is underpinned by the philosophy that each and every child should be parented – every day! In other words, children should not go through a day without an adult showing an interest in them and expressing a genuine concern for them. They all deserve to have an adult involved in guiding them and being a positive role model to them. We achieve this by having a large number of adults on duty in and around the Houses every day.
We are in a privileged position to have at least four adults (up to six on some nights), working in each boarding house every night; and we have an additional ten members of staff who live on site who are fully involved and committed to the boarders time at Hazlegrove. We all believe in promoting childhood and making sure that the children have a magical time whilst at Hazlegrove.
Communication is key and our “family-feel” encourages dialogue between all the adults involved with the care of the children. We would like parents to feel that they are a part of the boarding journey and that we work together to enrich the lives of the children in our care.

Pre-Prep Music and Drama
Great Stories Begin With Creativity.
At Hazlegrove, Music and Drama form a wonderfully enriching and crucial part of every child’s education. Curriculum music is taught from Nursery, with all children in the early years receiving inspiring and engaging music lessons every week. Lessons focus on sounds through multi-sensory, structured and sequential learning. By Year 2, children have developed a great awareness of pitch and rhythm, they can can sing in harmony and play basic patterns on instruments.
The Music Curriculum
Our music curriculum has been designed to support the extra-curricular learning of instruments as children move through the school. Children are introduced to our Music School through clubs from Year 1, where they can learn the basics of keyboards and classroom instruments, as well as sing in our pre-prep choir. Once children reach Year 2, they receive a full term of class violin lessons with one of our specialist teachers, it is always such an exciting time for the children.
Individual lessons with one of our 18 visiting instrumental teachers are available to Pre-Prep children as soon as they can manage 1-to-1 sessions. Pupils are encouraged to explore a variety of different options through our instrument trials, with opportunities for learning the piano, singing and a wide variety of orchestral instruments, as well as the drums, guitar, bagpipes and even DJing. We firmly believe that there is an instrument for everybody!
Those who learn an instrument (including during class music lessons), as well as those who sing in our choir, perform to parents and friends in our termly Pre-Prep concerts. We are always very proud of the standard of our young musicians!
Encouraging our young thespians!
Drama, too, forms a vital part of every Pre-Prep child’s Hazlegrove experience.
Weekly lessons are taught by our Head of Drama, who also plays a supporting role in all Pre-Prep productions. Our Pre-Prep productions provide opportunities for all children to experience performing to a rapt audience in our main theatre. Costumes and lighting are de rigeur, aiding our young actors in the display of key early skills, focus and confidence that will be developed further as they move through the school.

Key Stage 1 - Years 1 and 2
Key Stage 1 comprises of Years 1 and 2. Every class has a class teacher who cares and nurtures each individual child as well as providing them with a high-quality education and exciting opportunities amongst our exceptional facilities.
Giving the attention they need
Pre-Prep pupils have a busy morning, focussing on the academic subjects of English, Maths and Phonics, when pupils are full of energy and more able to concentrate. Children are taught in mixed ability classes by enthusiastic and inspiring teachers who differentiate to meet the needs of all children within their class. The effective use of our experienced Teaching Assistants ensures all children get individual attention.
Year 1 curriculum overview
Year 2 curriculum overview
Forest School
In the afternoons, children participate in practical subjects where they can be more hands-on. The school’s historic woods provide an undisturbed and inspiring setting for Forest School. Cooking over fires, problem solving and regular opportunities to develop confidence and self-esteem outside of the classroom, ensure that pupils develop a deep sense of appreciation of the natural world and a skillset that supports their learning within the classroom.
Learn More About Our Forest School
Specialist Teaching and Coaching
Specialist staff teach the children for subjects across the curriculum. From Nursery to Year 2, music is taught by our music staff. Year 1 and 2 pupils have a weekly drama session with our Head of Drama and are introduced to self-expression and improvisation as well as body awareness and movement in dance.
The Prep School PE staff teach all pupils in Reception and Key Stage 1 every week. A carousel of gymnastics, ball skills and games ensure that pupils have every opportunity to develop physical skills and coordination, as well as sowing the seed for a love of sport. Additionally, Pre-Prep pupils can access tennis coaching, golf lessons and ballet lessons in small groups throughout the year with our School tennis coach and professional golf and ballet teachers.

Years 3 and 4 Curriculum
Great Stories Begin With Curiosity...
Welcome to the Lower School at Hazlegrove! Through the curriculum, the children in Years 3 and 4 enjoy endless opportunities with plenty of scope for imagination as well as building resilience. Minds are unlocked, and doors are opened as the children progress along their educational journey and voyage of self-discovery, through to Middle School and beyond.
Education in Years 3 and 4
The nurturing environment fostered within the Lower School is centred around the belief that children learn best when they feel safe, happy, and confident. As children enter the Prep School aged 7, days are busy and varied, covering a broad and balanced curriculum. Lessons are engaging and stimulating.
Academic rigour is crucial, underpinning all elements of the Lower School curriculum, and children are closely monitored to ensure that all flourish, but not at the expense of the enjoyment of learning, or our school values, our cornerstones on which our ethos and endeavours are built.
Our Classrooms
Children make use of the expansive wider school facilities and specialist teaching in Science, French, Art, DT, Music, Drama, Computing, PE, Games and Outdoor Education. The children might find themselves discovering dragon eggs in our very own woods (we’re lucky the dragons keep coming back to lay, but we’re not sure which species they are!) and delving into dragon myths from around the world, then creating fantastical artwork, linking to their English non-chronological report writing. Or they are delving into the mysteries of Ancient Egypt, developing their understanding of instructional texts through the process of mumification (have you ever seen what happens to a mummified tomato?) before recreating living models of the River Nile and learning about rivers around the world in Geography.
...children are closely monitored to ensure that all flourish, but not at the expense of the enjoyment of learning, or our school values...
Our Specialist Teachers and Lessons
In both Year 3 and Year 4, lessons first thing in the morning are spent with the form tutor building solid foundations in Maths and English. Our passionate form tutors continue to support individual learning through Humanities, P.S.H.E and Wellbeing lessons. At this age, the children are taught in tutor groups which are parallel, mixed ability classes; Maths and spelling are the only lessons which are set at this age.
On a Monday, Year 3 could find themselves exploring ‘health related fitness’ in PE, linking to their Science ‘health and nutrition topic’ (it’s amazing the range of facial expressions a pair of tights being turned into food filled small intestines can invoke), then using their understanding of data handling from Maths to create a technology-based, informative presentation to a range of clients based up on their specific needs. On another day, children might be taking their parents on a tour of the Hazlegrove virtual Viking museum in the playground, designing and making games to show off their understanding of magnetism to share with younger pupils in the Pre-Prep, then later, taking an active role in a Philosophy4Children enquiry debating the difficulties of accidentally discovering an invisibility ring – If you know you won’t be caught, should you do whatever you like?
Through a creative cross-curricular approach, children are encouraged to see links between subjects and develop tools to join the dots between their skills, knowledge and understanding both between subjects and beyond, into their extra-curricular activities and personal development whilst appreciating the relevance of their experiences to the wider world. We aim to develop creative, curious, confident learners who are open-minded and caring.

Years 5 and 6 Curriculum
Great Stories Begin with the Extraordinary...
Years 5 and 6 are wonderful years - pupils’ minds are ripe for learning and absorbing new information like a sponge. At Hazlegrove, we take full advantage of this wonderful time!
We believe that a curriculum with a strong emphasis on practical skills and hands-on exploration develops a questioning nature in our pupils. Opportunities to further enrich and nurture curiosity through trips, visits and projects play a huge part in every child’s development at Hazlegrove.
Nurturing the Whole Child…
9, 10 and 11-year-olds are so able, and their teachers who know them well as individuals encourage them, and make the most of their creativity and their infectious enthusiasm to learn. Coupled with this is the need for support in areas that are still developing, which are different for each child and include physical, social, and emotional needs and skills, as well as a good grasp of their cognitive profile.
In a world that is constantly changing, a world where we are all racing to keep up, what we need is children who can face new challenges without fear or self-doubt. The world needs proactive and imaginative problem solvers who possess both the skills and the mental versatility to interpret new and unfamiliar problems quickly and then work independently and in small groups toward meaningful and robust solutions.
We are passionate about developing practical and effective problem-solving skills across all of our departments and constantly looking for new and exciting ways to emphasize the real-world applications and the relevance of the techniques the children are learning.
The Best of Both Worlds
We want the best of all worlds: the familiarity of one teacher knowing each child well but, equally, the opportunity to foster a greater sense of taking responsibility for personal organisation. This includes pupils looking after their own belongings, as they get older, moving around the site more independently, and learning key study skills as we set them prep to consolidate and extend the concepts learned in the classroom.
This is such an exciting time of development for children and is one where curiosity, creativity and confidence flourish at Hazlegrove.

Years 7 and 8 | The Upper School Curriculum
Great Stories Begin with the Inner Spark...
The Upper School at Hazlegrove is all about igniting the inner spark, helping children to discover and pursue their talents and providing an environment that allows them to flourish and reach their potential. Providing opportunities and responsibilities to all at the same time as reinforcing the key Hazlegrove values of Kindness, Grace, Courage, Integrity, Respect and Generosity.
Preparing for Senior School
The Upper School prepares children for the often challenging landscape of Senior School within an environment which recognises the very different needs of 11 and 12 year old children. We support those who decide to pursue a scholarship – it could be an Academic Scholarship or an Art, DT, Drama, Music, Sport or All Rounder – we have vast experience of helping and guiding those children through the process.
Here are just some of the things that we do differently in Upper School:
Our wellbeing programme and pastoral care actively address the issues which pre-teens face, with a full and broad reaching PHSE programme. Children at Hazlegrove's Upper School are well prepared for their next step which they can take with confidence and maturity at the age of 13.
An Environment for Learning and Support
At Hazlegrove, learning and enjoyment go together! There’s nothing better than getting our wellies on, planning where a new solar farm could go on the School site with all the calculations about energy, costs, area, size to make a brilliant maths lesson appeal to a whole range of different learning profiles in different ways. We know how to stretch children and support children, through the curriculum and our excellent Learning Support Unit, and most of all, we know our children well, being big enough to have specialists in all important areas of school life but small enough to be a close-knit team of staff who chat about the children and their needs every day.
Nothing gives us more pleasure than to receive emails from parents telling us that their child has progressed more during their time with us than they dared hope was possible and to see our children leave us on Speech Day ready, in every sense, for senior school and beyond.
We are so very proud of their achievements to date and Hazlegrove has been their constant and exceeded all expectations. Your team have all continued to sprinkle the 'magic dust' over the years that is the envy of other prep schools.

Inspection Reports
ISI Inspection Outcome
We are delighted to share the outcome of Hazlegrove’s recent Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) inspection.
We are very pleased to confirm that the school met all required standards, providing independent recognition of the quality of education, care and opportunities our pupils enjoy every day.
More than anything, we feel the report really captures what makes Hazlegrove special: a place where every child is known and supported as an individual, where academic ambition sits alongside a broad range of opportunities, and where confidence, kindness and curiosity are just as important as achievement.
A Broad and Inspiring Education
The inspectors highlighted the strength of our curriculum:
“Leaders ensure that the curriculum is broad, well planned and promotes respect and other British values while stimulating pupils’ curiosity and careful thinking.”
High-Quality Teaching
The report also reflects the strength of teaching across the school:
“Teaching is consistently engaging and well placed, enabling pupils to make good progress. Leaders and staff make effective use of assessments to identify pupils’ needs and evaluate their progress.”
Outstanding Pastoral Care
At the heart of Hazlegrove is our strong sense of care and community:
“Warm, supportive relationships between staff and pupils and effective pastoral support help to promote pupils’ confidence and sense of security across day and boarding communities.”
A Rich School Experience
The report celebrates the wide range of opportunities available beyond the classroom:

pageCache.pageTitle: Drama at Hazlegrove Prep | Hazlegrove School
pageCache.text:
Drama at Hazlegrove Prep
The Drama Department at Hazlegrove Prep School is a vibrant and dynamic hub of creativity, led by the dedicated and passionate Head of Drama, Miss Polly Agg-Manning. Under her expert guidance, the department has flourished, offering pupils of all ages the chance to immerse themselves in the world of performing arts. Whether it's acting, singing, or dancing, there is something for everyone to enjoy and explore.
Opportunities for All Ages
From the youngest pupils to those in their final year, every child at Hazlegrove is encouraged to participate in drama activities. The department is bustling with energy, providing a supportive environment where pupils can develop their talents and confidence. Each year, pupils have the opportunity to take part in major plays or musicals, ensuring that by the time they leave Hazlegrove, stepping onto the stage feels like second nature.
Drama Monitors in Year 8
For those in Year 8, there is a special opportunity to become a Drama Monitor. This role allows pupils to take on various responsibilities, such as helping backstage, managing costumes, and assisting with make-up. Being a Drama Monitor not only enhances their understanding of the theatrical process but also fosters leadership skills and teamwork.
Welcome to the Spotlight - our Head of Drama!
Polly attended The Royal Central School of Speech and Drama. She went on to study for a BA (Hons) in Drama and Education. Polly has had extensive experience in directing, having worked at Exeter Northcott Theatre and then as Head of Education at Hall for Cornwall. Polly has also worked at the BBC and has been a LAMDA teacher. Polly joined us from Blundell’s senior school, where she taught for seven years.
Encouraging Excellence
Hazlegrove is committed to nurturing the talents of pupils who show a particular aptitude for drama. These pupils are encouraged to apply for drama scholarships at their future schools, with the department providing guidance and support throughout the application process. The success of Hazlegrove's drama programme is evident in the numerous awards and scholarships received by its pupils from a wide range of prestigious senior schools.
A Thriving Community
The Drama Department at Hazlegrove is more than just a place to learn about performing arts; it is a thriving community where pupils can express themselves, build lasting friendships, and create unforgettable memories. The skills and experiences gained through drama at Hazlegrove prepare pupils not only for future academic endeavours but also for life beyond school, instilling confidence, creativity, and a love for the arts.
To nurture a child’s confidence is at the very heart of our drama programme.
Our well-appointed theatre provides ample opportunity for developing vocal skills, resilience, communication and curiosity. For those who see the world as a stage, this is a great place to start! Drama is taught as a part of the curriculum from Year 1 right the way through to Year 7, with a two-week production undertaken by the whole of Year 8 during the summer term.
Our purpose-built studio provides ample opportunity for keen dancers, with lessons taught to small groups throughout the whole school.
Speech & Drama: LAMDA and Scholarships
Speech & Drama is an optional extra and is a subject which can benefit children of all abilities, developing self-confidence, self-discipline and creativity. It can extend the most able, and offers all children an opportunity to excel.
Scholarships: Speech & Drama scholarship pupils are additionally offered individual coaching to help win both Drama and all-round scholarships.

Music at Hazelgrove Prep
Music and the Performing Arts are an integral part of life at Hazlegrove, with opportunities for every child both in and out of the classroom. Our pupils sing, play and perform in every year of their Hazlegrove journey, developing confidence and displaying our core values in all that they do.
Music at Hazlegrove
Our award-winning Music Department is vibrant and energetic, led by Director of Music and Performing Arts, Ms Becky Arch.
A love of music is forged throughout the school, with great opportunities for beginners through to more advanced musicians. All children sing with great enthusiasm and musicality, and we are very proud of the standard of our choirs, which form an integral part of our beautiful annual services at both Wells Cathedral and Sherborne Abbey. Parents and pupils alike enjoy spotting academic staff, who are a regular addition to our Hazlegrove Voices at these events!
Whilst in the classroom, children are introduced to music through imaginative and engaging topics from pop-song writing to the science of sound.
Singing in a choir is a part of the timetable from Years 3 to 6, and every child is encouraged to take up a musical instrument during their time at the school. Class-instrumental learning is taught in Years 2-6, as a part of the curriculum, with peripatetic staff supporting learning in brass, woodwind and strings.
Budding musicians are encouraged to join a wide variety of ensembles. There are opportunities for all and performances feature in our weekly informal Friday concerts as well as our whole-school and joint ventures throughout the year.
Music Ensembles and Instrumental Learning
The Music Department is an energetic and exciting place to be with ensembles such as our Senior and Junior Orchestras, Senior Strings, Hazlegroove Percussion Ensemble, Wind Band, DJ club and Senior Brass. Our six home-grown rock and pop bands are always extremely well received, with a recent group enjoying the opportunity to perform on local radio.
We offer an ever-growing selection of instruments taught by dedicated and inspirational staff, ranging from piano, singing and orchestral instruments to electric guitar and bass, bagpipes, percussion and drum kit. Our latest venture into individual and group DJing lessons has proved particularly popular!
Instrumental Lessons and Music Scholarships
All instrumental lessons are delivered on a rota system, ensuring that the impact on academic lessons is kept to a minimum. We work closely with our academic colleagues to ensure that subjects are not unduly affected, with leeway given for those receiving LSU support or those who are learning 3 or more instruments. Children are encouraged to work towards ABRSM and Trinity music exams, (although it is recognised that this is not always the best route for all!) and we also prepare a large number for Grade 5 Theory.
We have a strong tradition of music scholarships, with children receiving awards to a wide range of senior schools. All of our musicians are encouraged to explore their particular areas of interest, with recent pupils gaining recognition in the French horn, piano, composition and music technology.
Meet Our Director of Music and Performing Arts - Ms Arch!
Ms Arch trained as an Actor Musician at Rose Bruford College of Speech and Drama, graduating with a BA (Hons), before embarking on a successful performing career. She spent two years at the Royal National Theatre, appearing in Richard II alongside Fiona Shaw, and later performed in London's West End at the Apollo Theatre, as well as in repertory theatres across the UK.
Throughout her performing career, music remained at the heart of her work. Alongside acting, she taught cello, flute, piano, saxophone and singing, sharing her love of music with young people. In 2009 she moved into school teaching and has since inspired pupils in a variety of settings, including Downton Primary School, Walhampton School and Chafyn Grove School.
An accomplished choir leader, Ms Arch is passionate about helping children find confidence and joy through music. Her choirs have won the Salisbury Music Festival three times, reached the finals of the Barnardo's Choir of the Year competition and performed at the Barbican in London. She has also conducted concerts at Salisbury Cathedral on numerous occasions.
Outside the classroom, Ms Arch has played flute with the Salisbury Symphony Orchestra for many years and continues to enjoy singing with local choirs. She brings a wealth of professional experience, musical expertise and infectious enthusiasm to every rehearsal, lesson and performance at Hazlegrove.

Pastoral Care and Wellbeing
Great Stories Begin with Each Other... Nurturing the Whole Child.
The pastoral care of our children at Hazlegrove is at the heart of our ethos and all staff are involved and responsible for ensuring the children’s positive sense of self and wellbeing. The children are immersed in a caring community surrounded by adults who show respect and integrity in their daily interactions and who go out of their way to put the children first. Happy children are successful learners who have the confidence, resilience and humility to face and overcome challenges in their educational journeys.
A Tailored Pastoral Approach
Our tutors are the children’s greatest advocate; they are their first port of call at the start of every day and importantly, the first point of contact for parents. The tutors meet weekly to discuss pastoral issues, and the Pastoral Leadership Team (made up of the pastoral Heads of Pre-Prep, Lower School, Middle School, Upper School, the Head of Boarding, the Deputy Head and the School Psychologist) meet twice a week to discuss individual children and wider pastoral issues.
Guiding Our Children
Tutor times, assemblies, RE and PSHE lessons are the more formal avenues through which we support our children’s social and emotional development and guide them in their spiritual and moral journeys, helping them to become caring and conscientious global citizens. Our ‘Circle of Care’ shown above illustrates the depth and breadth of the pastoral support for our children at Hazlegrove.
Our dedicated and passionate staff model thoughtful and respectful behaviours and inspire our community to enact our values of integrity, courage, grace, kindness, generosity and respect which underpin all that we do at Hazlegrove.
We encourage and promote kindness through our school values; through assemblies and tutor time, Chapel and PSHE lessons. Friday Celebration Assembly provides a wonderful platform to celebrate acts of kindness and courage as well as other achievements throughout the week. We acknowledge specific examples of our school values through awards such as ‘Lower School Legend’, ‘Middle School Marvel’, ‘Upper School Good Egg’ and ‘Boarder of the Week’, and the Kindness cup is a much-coveted prize at our end of term Final assembly. Pre-Prep and Lower School further recognise and celebrate children who demonstrate our school values in their weekly section assemblies. Across the school we also have ‘Wise owls’ in Lower school, Middle School ‘Transformers’ and Upper School Monitors, specifically wellbeing monitors, who display generosity and kindness towards others.
Pastoral care never ends and is something that works its way through the fabric of our school and underpins everything we do at Hazlegrove.
Absolutely EXCELLENT pastoral care, treating every child's needs individually and going above and beyond with support and assistance when required.
